"""Two-tone spectroscopy of a SQUID transmon against flux, with the exact f01 and f02/2 drawn over the data (synthetic data)."""
import numpy as np

import scqfig as sq
from scqfig import physics as ph

TITLE = "Flux-tuned spectroscopy"
FAMILY = "Spectrum"


def build():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
    flux = np.linspace(-0.6, 0.6, 161)
    freq = np.linspace(3.2, 6.4, 241)
    f = ph.tunable_frequencies(flux, EJmax=18.0, EC=0.22, d=0.35, nlev=3)
    f01, f02h = f[:, 0], f[:, 1] / 2
    F, X = np.meshgrid(freq, flux, indexing="ij")
    line = lambda f0, w, A: A / (1 + ((F - f0[None, :]) / w) ** 2)
    S = line(f01, 0.02, 1.0) + line(f02h, 0.008, 0.45) + rng.normal(0, 0.04, F.shape)
    fig, ax = sq.figure("column", aspect=0.8)
    sq.plots.flux_spectroscopy(ax, flux, freq, S, model={r"$f_{01}$": f01, r"$f_{02}/2$": f02h})
    return fig


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sq.demo_main(build, __file__)

examples.caption: Vacuum-Rabi splitting: resonator transmission as a tunable qubit crosses it, with the bare modes dashed and 2g marked (synthetic data).
examples.code:
"""Vacuum-Rabi splitting: resonator transmission as a tunable qubit crosses it, with the bare modes dashed and 2g marked (synthetic data)."""
import numpy as np

import scqfig as sq
from scqfig import physics as ph

TITLE = "Avoided crossing"
FAMILY = "Spectrum"


def build():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(4)
    flux = np.linspace(0.18, 0.32, 141)
    freq = np.linspace(6.85, 7.15, 201)
    fq = ph.tunable_frequencies(flux, EJmax=40.0, EC=0.25, d=0.0, nlev=2)[:, 0]
    fr, g = 7.0, 0.035
    up, lo = ph.dressed_frequencies(fq, fr, g)
    theta = 0.5 * np.arctan2(2 * g, fq - fr)                 # photon weight of each normal mode
    w_lo, w_up = np.cos(theta) ** 2, np.sin(theta) ** 2
    F = freq[:, None]
    dip = lambda f0, w: w / (1 + ((F - f0[None, :]) / 0.004) ** 2)
    S = 1 - 0.85 * (dip(lo, w_up) + dip(up, w_lo)) + rng.normal(0, 0.015, (freq.size, flux.size))
    x0 = flux[np.argmin(np.abs(fq - fr))]
    fig, ax = sq.figure("column", aspect=0.8)
    sq.plots.avoided_crossing(ax, flux, freq, S, bare=(fq, np.full_like(flux, fr)), g=g, x0=x0)
    return fig


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sq.demo_main(build, __file__)

examples.title: Black-box quantization
examples.caption: Black-box quantization of the transmon and readout resonator of example 72: (a) the susceptance the junction sees, whose rising zeros are the modes and whose slopes set their impedances; (b) the first-order Kerr matrix, with exact diagonalization of the same circuit in brackets (computed).
examples.code:
"""Black-box quantization of the transmon and readout resonator of example 72: (a) the susceptance the junction sees, whose rising zeros are the modes and whose slopes set their impedances; (b) the first-order Kerr matrix, with exact diagonalization of the same circuit in brackets (computed)."""
import numpy as np

import scqfig as sq
from scqfig import physics as ph

TITLE = "Black-box quantization"
FAMILY = "Design"

# example 72's device; the 50 ohm feedline is small beside the 2.8 kohm of C_kappa, so it counts as ground
C_SIGMA, C_G, C_R, C_K, L_J, F_R = 85e-15, 5e-15, 400e-15, 8e-15, 10e-9, 7.0e9
L_R = 1 / ((2 * np.pi * F_R) ** 2 * C_R)


def build():
    C = np.array([[C_SIGMA, -C_G], [-C_G, C_R + C_K + C_G]])         # transmon node, resonator node
    Linv = np.diag([1 / L_J, 1 / L_R])                                 # the junction as its linear inductance
    B = lambda f: ph.port_susceptance(f, C, Linv)
    bb = ph.black_box(B, ph.ej_from_lj(L_J), np.linspace(1, 20, 2001))
    exact = ph.transmon_resonator(C_SIGMA - C_G, C_G, C_R + C_K, L_J, L_R)
    f = np.linspace(4.0, 8.0, 2001)
    fig, (a, b) = sq.figure("page", aspect=0.3, ncols=2, gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [2.4, 1]})
    sq.plots.admittance(a, f, B(f), modes=bb, labels=["q", "r"])
    sq.plots.kerr_matrix(b, bb["K"], ["q", "r"], exact=exact["K"], cbar=False)
    b.set_xlabel("MHz, exact in brackets")
    sq.panel(a, "a")
    sq.panel(b, "b")
    return fig


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sq.demo_main(build, __file__)

import scqfig as sq
from scqfig import physics as ph
from scqfig.plots.design import collision_windows

TITLE = "Frequency lines"
FAMILY = "Design"


def build():
    EJ, EC = {"Q1": 13.2, "Q2": 15.8, "Q3": 18.6}, 0.22              # GHz
    qubits = {}
    for name, ej in EJ.items():
        f = ph.transmon_spectrum(ej, EC, nlev=3)
        qubits[name] = (f[1], f[2] - f[1])                            # (f01, f12)
    f1, f12 = qubits["Q1"]
    windows = [(f1 + c - w, f1 + c + w) for _, c, w, _ in collision_windows(f12 - f1)]   # where Q2 must not sit
    fig, ax = sq.figure("page", aspect=0.24)
    sq.plots.frequency_lines(ax, qubits, resonators={"R1": 6.85, "R2": 6.95, "R3": 7.05}, spread=0.04,
                             scans={"Q2": (qubits["Q2"][0], f1 + 0.3)}, windows=windows,
                             bands={"Purcell filter": (6.75, 7.15)}, floor=ph.thermal_frequency(1e-3, 0.02),
                             guides={"box mode": 7.6}, mass_axis=True, xlim=(2.6, 8.0))
    return fig

"""Notch-resonator transmission as magnitude, phase and circle, with one complex fit and the cable delay, amplitude and phase calibrated out (synthetic data)."""
import numpy as np

import scqfig as sq
from scqfig import physics as ph

TITLE = "S21 of a resonator"
FAMILY = "Readout"


def build():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(20)
    fr, Qi, Qc, phi = 6.8312, 3.0e4, 1.5e4, 0.12
    Ql = 1 / (1 / Qi + np.cos(phi) / Qc)
    f = np.linspace(fr - 6 * fr / Ql, fr + 6 * fr / Ql, 161)
    s = ph.notch_s21(f, fr, Ql, Qc, phi, a=0.42, alpha=1.1, tau=45.0)          # tau in ns, f in GHz
    s = s + 0.42 * 0.006 * (rng.standard_normal(f.size) + 1j * rng.standard_normal(f.size))
    r = sq.fit.notch(f, s)
    fig, ax = sq.figure("page", aspect=0.4)
    ax.remove()
    axd = fig.subplot_mosaic([["mag", "circle"], ["phase", "circle"]], width_ratios=[1.55, 1])
    axd["phase"].sharex(axd["mag"])
    sq.plots.s21_magnitude(axd["mag"], f, s, fit=r)
    sq.plots.s21_phase(axd["phase"], f, s, fit=r)
    sq.plots.s21_circle(axd["circle"], f, s, fit=r)
    axd["mag"].set_xlabel("")
    axd["mag"].tick_params(labelbottom=False)
    for k, name in zip("abc", ("mag", "phase", "circle")):
        sq.panel(axd[name], k)
    return fig

    sq.demo_main(build, __file__)

"""Dispersive readout: resonator transmission with the qubit in |0> and in |1>, the 2chi shift computed for g = 85 MHz and Delta = -2.09 GHz, and the readout frequency between the two dips (synthetic data)."""
import numpy as np

import scqfig as sq
from scqfig import physics as ph

TITLE = "Dispersive readout"
FAMILY = "Readout"


def build():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(22)
    fr, fq, g, alpha = 7.15, 5.06, 0.085, -0.233
    chi = ph.dispersive_shift(fq, fr, g, alpha)                    # GHz, negative here
    Ql, Qi = fr / (2 * abs(chi)), 3e5                              # kappa = 2|chi|
    Qc = 1 / (1 / Ql - 1 / Qi)
    f = np.linspace(fr - 0.003, fr + 0.003, 121)

    def noise():
        return 0.012 * (rng.standard_normal(f.size) + 1j * rng.standard_normal(f.size))

import numpy as np

import scqfig as sq
from scqfig.plots.timedomain import tls_t1

TITLE = "TLS spectral diffusion"
FAMILY = "Time domain"


def build():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(37)
    hours = np.linspace(0, 24, 97)
    freq = np.linspace(5.10, 5.30, 201)                  # GHz
    f0 = np.array([5.122, 5.163, 5.191, 5.243, 5.271])   # defect centres (GHz)
    drift = np.cumsum(rng.normal(0, 0.7, (hours.size, f0.size)), axis=0)        # random walk (MHz)
    drift += 3.5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * hours[:, None] / rng.uniform(8, 20, f0.size) + rng.uniform(0, 6, f0.size))

    tracks = f0 + 1e-3 * drift                           # shape (time, defect)

    gamma = np.array([1.2, 0.8, 1.5, 1.0, 1.2])          # defect decoherence gamma/2pi (MHz)
    T1 = tls_t1(freq[:, None], tracks, g=g, gamma=gamma, t1_bg=80.0)
    T1 = T1 * rng.normal(1, 0.07, T1.shape)
    fig, ax = sq.figure("column", aspect=0.78)

"""Two-qubit tomography of the Bell state (|00> + |11>)/sqrt(2): real and imaginary parts of the reconstructed density matrix (synthetic data)."""
import numpy as np

import scqfig as sq
from scqfig import physics as ph

TITLE = "Density matrix"
FAMILY = "States"


def noisy_bell(seed=42):
    """A Bell state with depolarising, dephasing and tomography noise, projected onto a physical state."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    bell = ph.dm(np.array([1, 0, 0, 1]) / np.sqrt(2))
    rho = 0.92 * bell + 0.08 * np.eye(4) / 4
    rho[0, 3] *= np.exp(0.12j)
    rho[3, 0] = rho[0, 3].conj()
    H = rng.normal(0, 0.012, (4, 4)) + 1j * rng.normal(0, 0.012, (4, 4))
    rho = rho + (H + H.conj().T) / 2
    w, V = np.linalg.eigh(rho)
    w = np.clip(w, 0, None)
    rho = (V * w) @ V.conj().T
    return rho / np.trace(rho).real, bell


def build():
    rho, _ = noisy_bell()
    fig, axes = sq.figure("column", aspect=0.52, ncols=2)
    sq.plots.density_matrix(axes, rho)
    return fig

"""Kinetic-mixing reach of a qubit dark-photon search against frequency for one and sixteen sensors at 20 and 50 mK, from an illustrative counting model with thermal dark counts, an excluded region and a synthetic measured limit, with the dark-photon mass on the top axis (computed)."""
import numpy as np

import scqfig as sq
from scqfig import physics as ph

TITLE = "Dark-photon reach"
FAMILY = "Dark matter"


def counting_reach(f, n_q, T, tau=100e-6, t_point=3600.0, p_readout=1e-3, eps0=1e-10, f0=5.0):
    """Smallest coupling whose signal clears max(3, 5 sqrt(dark counts)) in t_point seconds of
    tau-long shots on n_q sensors. The excitation probability per shot grows as eps^2 f, reaching one
    at eps0 for a sensor at f0 GHz; dark counts come from readout error and thermal population."""
    shots = n_q * t_point / tau
    dark = (p_readout + ph.thermal_population(f, T)) * shots
    p_needed = np.maximum(3.0, 5.0 * np.sqrt(dark)) / shots
    return eps0 * np.sqrt(p_needed * f0 / f)


def build():
    t = sq.theme()
    f = np.logspace(0, 1, 200)                                      # GHz
    curves, styles = {}, {}
    for n_q, colour in ((1, t.cycle[0]), (16, t.cycle[1])):
        for T, ls in ((0.02, "-"), (0.05, (0, (4, 2)))):
            name = rf"$n_q$ = {n_q}, {T * 1e3:.0f} mK"
            curves[name] = counting_reach(f, n_q, T)
            styles[name] = dict(color=colour, ls=ls)
    fig, ax = sq.figure("column", aspect=0.85)
    sq.plots.reach(ax, f, curves, styles=styles, excluded="above", limits={"pilot run": (6.2, 4e-12)},
                   loc="lower left")

"""Lumped circuit of a transmon coupled to a quarter-wave readout resonator on a feedline, each Hamiltonian term on the tile of the element that produces it."""
import numpy as np

import scqfig as sq
from scqfig import physics as ph
from scqfig.schematics import symbols as S

TITLE = "Transmon and readout circuit"
FAMILY = "Schematics"

H_PLANCK, E, PHI0 = 6.62607015e-34, 1.602176634e-19, 2.067833848e-15
C_SIGMA, L_J, C_G, C_R, C_K, F_R = 85e-15, 10e-9, 5e-15, 400e-15, 8e-15, 7.0e9


def values():
    """Circuit parameters to energies (GHz): E_C, E_J, the exact f01, L_r for f_r, and g."""
    EC = E ** 2 / (2 * C_SIGMA) / H_PLANCK / 1e9
    EJ = (PHI0 / (2 * np.pi)) ** 2 / L_J / H_PLANCK / 1e9
    f01 = ph.transmon_spectrum(EJ, EC)[1]
    L_R = 1 / ((2 * np.pi * F_R) ** 2 * C_R)
    g = 0.5 * C_G / np.sqrt(C_SIGMA * C_R) * np.sqrt(f01 * F_R / 1e9)
    return EC, EJ, f01, L_R, g


def build():
    t = sq.theme()
    EC, EJ, f01, L_R, g = values()
    fig, ax = sq.figure("column", aspect=0.69, layout=None)
    ax.set_position([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0])
    S.blank(ax)
    fs = t.size - 0.5
    qc, rc = t.qubits[0], t.bus
    yf, yt, yb = 3.3, 2.0, 0.6                                   # feedline, top rail, ground rail

    # feedline from a source to a matched load
    S.wire(ax, [0.4, 6.0], [yf, yf])
    S.wire(ax, [0.4, 0.4], [yf, 2.9])
    S.ac_source(ax, 0.4, 2.75, r=0.15)
    S.wire(ax, [0.4, 0.4], [2.6, 2.35])
    S.ground(ax, 0.4, 2.35)
    S.wire(ax, [6.0, 6.0], [yf, 3.0])
    S.resistor_v(ax, 6.0, 3.0, 2.5)
    S.wire(ax, [6.0, 6.0], [2.5, 2.35])
    S.ground(ax, 6.0, 2.35)
    ax.text(0.62, 2.75, "in", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=fs)
    ax.text(5.8, 2.75, r"$Z_0$ = 50 Ω", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=fs)

    with S.tiles():
        # coupling to the feedline: a port, not a Hamiltonian term, so no tile
        S.node(ax, 1.8, yf)
        S.wire(ax, [1.8, 1.8], [yf, 2.655])
        S.capacitor_v(ax, 1.8, 2.62, tile_kind=False)
        S.wire(ax, [1.8, 1.8], [2.585, yt])
        ax.text(1.97, 2.62, rf"$C_\kappa$ = {C_K * 1e15:.0f} fF", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=fs)

        # resonator: L_r and C_r share one tile, the term h f_r a+a
        S.tile(ax, 1.8, 1.3, 1.5, 1.75, sq.lighten(rc, 0.86))
        S.wire(ax, [1.2, 2.4], [yt, yt], color=rc)
        S.wire(ax, [1.2, 2.4], [yb, yb], color=rc)
        S.wire(ax, [1.2, 1.2], [yt, 1.75], color=rc)
        S.inductor_v(ax, 1.2, 1.75, 0.85, color=rc, tile_kind=False)
        S.wire(ax, [1.2, 1.2], [0.85, yb], color=rc)
        S.wire(ax, [2.4, 2.4], [yt, 1.335], color=rc)
        S.capacitor_v(ax, 2.4, 1.3, color=rc, tile_kind=False)
        S.wire(ax, [2.4, 2.4], [1.265, yb], color=rc)
        S.node(ax, 1.8, yt, color=rc)
        S.node(ax, 2.4, yt, color=rc)
        S.wire(ax, [1.8, 1.8], [yb, 0.45], color=rc)
        S.ground(ax, 1.8, 0.45, color=rc)
        ax.text(0.98, 1.3, r"$L_r$" + "\n" + f"{L_R * 1e9:.2f} nH", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=fs, color=rc)
        ax.text(2.56, 1.3, r"$C_r$" + "\n" + f"{C_R * 1e15:.0f} fF", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=fs, color=rc)

        # coupling capacitor, the term h g n (a + a+)
        S.wire(ax, [2.4, 3.415], [yt, yt])
        S.capacitor_h(ax, 3.45, yt, tile_kind="coupling")
        S.wire(ax, [3.485, 4.2], [yt, yt])
        ax.text(3.45, yt + 0.27, rf"$C_g$ = {C_G * 1e15:.0f} fF", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=fs)

        # transmon: junction (nonlinear tile) and shunt capacitor (capacitive tile)
        S.wire(ax, [4.2, 5.6], [yt, yt], color=qc)
        S.wire(ax, [4.2, 5.6], [yb, yb], color=qc)
        S.wire(ax, [4.2, 4.2], [yt, yb], color=qc)
        S.junction(ax, 4.2, 1.3)
        S.wire(ax, [5.6, 5.6], [yt, 1.335], color=qc)
        S.capacitor_v(ax, 5.6, 1.3, color=qc)
        S.wire(ax, [5.6, 5.6], [1.265, yb], color=qc)
        S.node(ax, 4.2, yt, color=qc)
        S.wire(ax, [4.9, 4.9], [yb, 0.45], color=qc)
        S.ground(ax, 4.9, 0.45, color=qc)
        ax.text(4.0, 1.3, r"$L_J$" + "\n" + f"{L_J * 1e9:.0f} nH", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=fs)
        ax.text(5.4, 1.3, r"$C_\Sigma$" + "\n" + f"{C_SIGMA * 1e15:.0f} fF", ha="right", va="center",
                fontsize=fs, color=qc)

    # the Hamiltonian, one tile per term, each tile the colour of the element behind it
    terms = [(r"$4E_C\hat n^2$", rf"$E_C/h$ = {EC * 1e3:.0f} MHz", "capacitive"),
             (r"$-E_J\cos\hat\varphi$", rf"$E_J/h$ = {EJ:.1f} GHz", "nonlinear"),
             (r"$hf_r\hat a^\dagger\hat a$", rf"$f_r$ = {F_R / 1e9:.2f} GHz", sq.lighten(rc, 0.86)),
             (r"$hg\,\hat n(\hat a+\hat a^\dagger)$", rf"$g/h$ = {g * 1e3:.0f} MHz", "coupling")]
    ax.set_xlim(-0.1, 6.5)
    ax.set_ylim(-0.95, 3.5)
    ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="box")
    ax.apply_aspect()
    r = fig.canvas.get_renderer()
    inv = ax.transData.inverted()

    def width(s, size):
        txt = ax.text(0, 0, s, fontsize=size)
        bb = inv.transform(txt.get_window_extent(r))
        txt.remove()
        return bb[1, 0] - bb[0, 0]

    big, small, pad, plus = fs + 0.5, fs - 1.5, 0.14, 0.26
    tiles = [max(width(a, big), width(b, small)) + pad for a, b, _ in terms]
    head = width(r"$\hat H =$", big) + 0.1
    x = 3.2 - (head + sum(tiles) + plus * (len(tiles) - 1)) / 2          # the row centred under the circuit
    y = -0.45
    ax.text(x, y + 0.08, r"$\hat H =$", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=big)
    x += head
    for k, ((term, val, kind), w) in enumerate(zip(terms, tiles)):
        S.tile(ax, x + w / 2, y - 0.03, w, 0.66, kind, z=1)
        ax.text(x + w / 2, y + 0.08, term, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=big, zorder=3)
        ax.text(x + w / 2, y - 0.2, val, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=small, color=t.reference, zorder=3)
        x += w
        if k < len(terms) - 1:
            ax.text(x + plus / 2, y + 0.08, "+", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=big)
            x += plus
    ax.text(4.9, 0.14, rf"$f_{{01}}$ = {f01:.2f} GHz", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=fs - 1, color=t.reference)
    return fig


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sq.demo_main(build, __file__)

"""Transmon ladder (E_J/E_C = 40) to scale, with drive photons for f01, f12 and the two-photon f02/2, and the parity-forbidden single-photon 0-2 transition."""
import scqfig as sq
from scqfig import physics as ph
from scqfig.schematics import motifs, symbols

TITLE = "Level ladder and transitions"
FAMILY = "Schematics"

EJ, EC = 12.0, 0.30                                           # GHz


def build():
    t = sq.theme()
    E = ph.transmon_spectrum(EJ, EC, nlev=3)                   # [0, f01, f02], computed in the charge basis
    f01, f02 = E[1], E[2]
    fig, ax = sq.figure("column", aspect=0.78)
    symbols.blank(ax)
    fs = t.size - 0.5
    x0, x1 = 0.3, 14.4
    c = [2.5, 6.1, 9.7, 13.0]                                  # transition columns
    gap = (c[2] - 1.05, c[2] + 1.05)                           # |1> gives way to the virtual level here
    for n, En in enumerate(E):
        segs = [(x0, gap[0]), (gap[1], x1)] if n == 1 else [(x0, x1)]
        for a, b in segs:
            motifs.ladder(ax, a, b, [En], colors=[t.levels[n]])
        ax.text(x1 + 0.3, En, rf"$|{n}\rangle$", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=fs + 0.5, color=t.levels[n])

    def photon(xc, y, f, label=None):
        motifs.wavy(ax, (xc - 2.3, y), (xc - 0.22, y), amp=0.2, waves=f / 1.25, lw=1.0, head=0.4)
        if label:
            ax.text(xc - 1.3, y + 0.4, label, ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=fs - 0.5, color=t.signal,
                    linespacing=1.15)

    def ghz(f):
        return f"{f:.2f} GHz"

    motifs.transition(ax, (c[0], 0), (c[0], f01))
    photon(c[0], f01 / 2, f01, r"$f_{01}$" + "\n" + ghz(f01))
    motifs.transition(ax, (c[1], f01), (c[1], f02))
    photon(c[1], (f01 + f02) / 2, f02 - f01, r"$f_{12}$" + "\n" + ghz(f02 - f01))
    ax.plot([c[2] - 0.9, c[2] + 0.9], [f02 / 2] * 2, color=t.reference, lw=0.9, ls=(0, (3, 2)), zorder=3)
    ax.text(c[2] + 0.95, f02 / 2 - 0.2, "virtual", ha="left", va="top", fontsize=fs - 1.5, color=t.reference)
    motifs.transition(ax, (c[2], 0), (c[2], f02 / 2))
    motifs.transition(ax, (c[2], f02 / 2), (c[2], f02))
    photon(c[2], f02 / 4, f02 / 2, r"$f_{02}/2$" + "\n" + ghz(f02 / 2))
    photon(c[2], 3 * f02 / 4, f02 / 2)
    motifs.transition(ax, (c[3], 0), (c[3], f02), allowed=False)
    photon(c[3], f02 / 4, f02, r"$f_{02}$" + "\n" + ghz(f02))
    ax.text(c[3] + 0.3, f02 * 0.75, "forbidden", rotation=90, ha="left", va="center", fontsize=fs - 1.5, color=t.ink)
    sq.note(ax, rf"$E_J/E_C$ = {EJ / EC:.0f},  $\alpha/h$ = {(f02 - 2 * f01) * 1e3:.0f} MHz".replace("-", "−"), loc="upper left",
            color=t.reference)
    ax.set_xlim(-0.2, x1 + 1.3)
    ax.set_ylim(-0.6, f02 + 1.5)
    return fig


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sq.demo_main(build, __file__)

import numpy as np
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch

import scqfig as sq
from scqfig.schematics import motifs, symbols

TITLE = "Qubit array in a uniform field"
FAMILY = "Schematics"


def build():
    t = sq.theme()
    rng = np.random.default_rng(77)
    rows, cols = 3, 4
    excited = set(rng.choice(rows * cols, 3, replace=False).tolist())
    fig, ax = sq.figure("column", aspect=0.72)
    symbols.blank(ax)
    x0, y0, w, h = -0.6, -0.6, cols - 1 + 1.2, rows - 1 + 1.2
    ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((x0, y0), w, h, boxstyle="round,pad=0,rounding_size=0.18", fc=t.wash, ec="none",
                                zorder=1))
    for k in range(rows * cols):
        x, y = k % cols, rows - 1 - k // cols
        up = k not in excited
        hgt = 0.62 if up else -0.62
        motifs.spin(ax, x, y - hgt / 2, hgt, color=t.qubits[0] if up else t.qubits[1], lw=1.8)
    for p0, p1 in (((-1.1, 3.4), (-0.3, 2.7)), ((-1.85, 1.0), (-0.7, 1.0)), ((1.25, 3.68), (1.55, 2.7)),
                   ((4.55, 3.25), (3.7, 2.35)), ((4.65, -0.55), (3.7, 0.1))):                  # all end at the wash

import scqfig as sq
from scqfig.schematics import QCircuit

TITLE = "Teleportation and gate glyphs"
FAMILY = "Schematics"


def teleport():
    c = QCircuit(3, labels=[r"$|\psi\rangle$", r"$|0\rangle$", r"$|0\rangle$"], outputs=[None, None, r"$|\psi\rangle$"])
    c.gate("H", 1)
    c.cnot(1, 2)
    c.group([1, 2], cols=(0, 1), label="Bell pair")
    c.slice()
    c.cnot(0, 1)
    c.gate("H", 0)
    c.measure([0, 1])
    c.gate("X", 2, cond=1)
    c.gate("Z", 2, cond=0)
    return c


def glyphs():
    c = QCircuit(3, labels=[r"$q_0$", r"$q_1$", r"$q_2$"])
    c.gate(r"$R_x(\pi/2)$", 0)
    c.gate("T", 1)
    c.controlled("U", [0], 2, open_controls=[1])
    c.cz(0, 1)
    c.swap(1, 2)
    c.multi("V", [0, 1, 2])
    c.measure(2)
    return c


def build():
    a, b = teleport(), glyphs()
    (wa, ha), (wb, hb) = a.figsize(), b.figsize()
    fig, (ax_a, ax_b) = sq.figure(max(wa, wb), height=ha + hb + 0.25, nrows=2,
                                  gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [ha, hb]})
    a.draw(ax_a)
    b.draw(ax_b)

"""Black-box quantization in four steps for the device of example 72: (a) the transmon coupled to its readout resonator; (b) the junction split into its linear inductance and its nonlinear remainder; (c) the linear part as one admittance, probed by a swept current source; (d) that admittance beside the nonlinear element, whose zero-point phase each mode sets (computed)."""
import numpy as np

import scqfig as sq
from scqfig import physics as ph
from scqfig.schematics import symbols as S

TITLE = "Black-box circuit"
FAMILY = "Schematics"

C_SIGMA, C_G, C_R, C_K, L_J, F_R = 85e-15, 5e-15, 400e-15, 8e-15, 10e-9, 7.0e9   # example 72's device
L_R = 1 / ((2 * np.pi * F_R) ** 2 * C_R)
YT, YM, YB = 1.75, 1.1, 0.45                                     # top rail, element centres, ground rail


def branch(ax, x, draw, color=None):
    """A vertical branch from the top rail to the ground rail with an element drawn at YM."""
    S.wire(ax, [x, x], [YT, YM + 0.3], color=color)
    S.wire(ax, [x, x], [YM - 0.3, YB], color=color)
    draw(x)


def capacitor(ax, x, color=None):
    S.wire(ax, [x, x], [YT, YM + 0.035], color=color)
    S.capacitor_v(ax, x, YM, color=color)
    S.wire(ax, [x, x], [YM - 0.035, YB], color=color)


def network(ax, t, fs, split):
    """Resonator, coupling capacitor and transmon; split replaces the junction by L_J and the
    nonlinear element."""
    rc, qc = t.bus, t.qubits[0]
    branch(ax, 0.35, lambda x: S.inductor_v(ax, x, YM + 0.3, YM - 0.3, color=rc), rc)
    capacitor(ax, 0.85, rc)
    for y in (YT, YB):
        S.wire(ax, [0.35, 0.85], [y, y], color=rc)
    S.wire(ax, [0.85, 1.315], [YT, YT])
    S.capacitor_h(ax, 1.35, YT, tile_kind="coupling")
    S.wire(ax, [1.385, 1.85], [YT, YT])
    S.wire(ax, [0.85, 1.85], [YB, YB])
    capacitor(ax, 1.85, qc)
    right = 3.05 if split else 2.5
    for y in (YT, YB):
        S.wire(ax, [1.85, right], [y, y], color=qc)
    if split:
        branch(ax, 2.5, lambda x: S.inductor_v(ax, x, YM + 0.3, YM - 0.3), qc)
        S.wire(ax, [3.05, 3.05], [YT, YB], color=qc)
        S.nonlinear_element(ax, 3.05, YM)
    else:
        S.wire(ax, [2.5, 2.5], [YT, YB], color=qc)
        S.junction(ax, 2.5, YM)
    S.ground(ax, 1.35, YB - 0.08)
    S.wire(ax, [1.35, 1.35], [YB, YB - 0.08])
    lab = dict(fontsize=fs, va="center")
    ax.text(0.2, YM, r"$L_r$", ha="right", color=rc, **lab)
    ax.text(1.0, YM, r"$C_r$", ha="left", color=rc, **lab)
    ax.text(1.35, YT + 0.22, r"$C_g$", ha="center", **lab)
    ax.text(2.0, YM, r"$C_\Sigma$", ha="left", color=qc, **lab)
    ax.text(2.65 if split else 2.68, YM, r"$L_J$", ha="left", **lab)
    if split:
        ax.text(3.05, YM - 0.42, "nl", ha="center", **lab)


def black_box(ax, fs, x=2.6):
    """The linear part as one admittance, its port on the rails at x."""
    S.admittance_box(ax, 0.95, YM, w=1.1, h=0.62, fs=fs + 1)
    for y, side in ((YT, YM + 0.31), (YB, YM - 0.31)):
        S.wire(ax, [0.95, 0.95], [side, y])
        S.wire(ax, [0.95, x], [y, y])


def build():
    t = sq.theme()
    fs = t.size - 1.5
    C = np.array([[C_SIGMA, -C_G], [-C_G, C_R + C_K + C_G]])
    bb = ph.black_box(lambda f: ph.port_susceptance(f, C, np.diag([1 / L_J, 1 / L_R])), ph.ej_from_lj(L_J),
                      np.linspace(1, 20, 2001))
    fig, axes = sq.figure("column", aspect=0.7, nrows=2, ncols=2)
    for ax, k, ylim in zip(axes.flat, "abcd", [(0.2, 2.1)] * 2 + [(0.05, 1.9)] * 2):
        S.blank(ax)
        ax.set_xlim(-0.05, 3.45)
        ax.set_ylim(*ylim)
        sq.panel(ax, k)
    a, b, c, d = axes.flat
    with S.tiles():
        network(a, t, fs, split=False)
        network(b, t, fs, split=True)

    black_box(c, fs)
    S.wire(c, [2.6, 2.6], [YT, YM + 0.13])
    S.wire(c, [2.6, 2.6], [YM - 0.13, YB])
    S.current_source(c, 2.6, YM, up=True)
    S.tunable_mark(c, 2.6, YM, size=0.42)
    c.text(2.85, YM, r"$I(\omega)$", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=fs)
    c.text(1.75, 0.18, r"$Y(\omega) = I/V$", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=fs)

    with S.tiles():
        black_box(d, fs)
        S.wire(d, [2.6, 2.6], [YT, YB])
        S.nonlinear_element(d, 2.6, YM)
    S.flux_arrow(d, (2.82, YM + 0.25), (2.82, YM - 0.25), rad=-0.5, label=r"$\varphi_\mathrm{zpf}$",
                 offset=(0.36, 0.0))
    modes = ", ".join(rf"$\varphi_{n}$ = {p:.2g}" for n, p in zip("qr", bb["phi"]))
    d.text(1.75, 0.18, modes, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=fs)
    return fig


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sq.demo_main(build, __file__)

"""A generic transmon design recipe in eight numbered steps: each box holds instruction lines, a mini-plot from toy models and the tools the step uses, arrows run through the grid and two optional steps sit in dashed boxes below."""
import numpy as np

import scqfig as sq

TITLE = "Recipe grid"
FAMILY = "Schematics"


def band(ax):
    t = sq.theme()
    ax.axvspan(4.0, 6.0, color=t.tint, lw=0)
    for f in (4.8, 5.3):
        ax.plot([f, f], [0.1, 0.55], color=t.qubits[0], lw=1.1)
    ax.plot([7.2, 7.2], [0.45, 0.9], color=t.bus, lw=1.1)
    ax.set(xlim=(3.5, 8.0), ylim=(0, 1), yticks=[], xticks=[4, 6, 8], xlabel="GHz")


def junction(ax):
    ej = np.linspace(8, 30, 100)
    ax.plot(ej, np.sqrt(8 * ej * 0.25) - 0.25, **sq.model_kw())
    ax.plot(16, np.sqrt(8 * 16 * 0.25) - 0.25, **sq.sim_kw(ms=3.5))
    ax.set(xlim=(8, 30), xticks=[10, 20, 30], yticks=[4, 6], xlabel=r"$E_J/h$ (GHz)")


def hamiltonian(ax):
    sq.schematics.text_panel(ax, [r"$H/h=f_q\,b^\dagger b+\frac{\alpha}{2}\,b^{\dagger2}b^2$",
                                  r"$+\,f_r\,a^\dagger a+g\,(a^\dagger b+ab^\dagger)$"])


def readout(ax):
    f = np.linspace(-3, 2, 400)
    for f0, c in ((0.0, sq.theme().ink), (-1.6, sq.theme().accent)):
        ax.plot(f, 1 - 0.9 / (1 + ((f - f0) / 0.25) ** 2), color=c, lw=0.9)
    ax.set(xlim=(-3, 2), ylim=(0, 1.08), yticks=[], xticks=[-2, 0], xlabel=r"$f-f_r$ (MHz)")


def losses(ax):
    t = sq.theme()
    ax.bar(range(3), [60, 140, 42], 0.6, color=["white", "white", t.light], ec=t.ink, lw=0.5, log=True)
    ax.set(ylim=(5, 500), xticks=range(3), xticklabels=["TLS", "P", "sum"], ylabel=r"$T_1$ ($\mu$s)")
    ax.minorticks_off()


def spread(ax):
    rn = np.linspace(-4, 4, 200)
    ax.fill_between(rn, np.exp(-rn ** 2 / 2), color=sq.theme().light, lw=0)
    ax.plot(rn, np.exp(-rn ** 2 / 2), **sq.model_kw())
    ax.set(xlim=(-4, 4), ylim=(0, 1.15), yticks=[], xticks=[-3, 0, 3], xlabel=r"$\delta R_n$ (%)")


def validate(ax):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
    for i in range(3):
        ax.plot(i + rng.uniform(-0.2, 0.2, 8), 1 + rng.normal(0, 0.03 * (i + 1), 8), **sq.data_kw(ms=2.5))
    ax.axhline(1, **sq.ref_kw())
    ax.set(xlim=(-0.5, 2.5), xticks=range(3), xticklabels=["$f$", "$g$", r"$\chi$"], ylim=(0.8, 1.2),
           yticks=[0.9, 1.0, 1.1], ylabel="pred./meas.")


def build():
    steps = [
        dict(title="Specify", lines=["Fix the band, the readout", "and the lifetime goals."], panel=band,
             tools=["pen", "paper"]),
        dict(title="Junction", lines=[r"Pick $E_J$ for the target", r"$f_{01}$ at fixed $E_C$."], panel=junction,
             tools=["pen", "code"]),
        dict(title="Capacitances", lines=["Solve the Maxwell matrix;", r"read $E_C$ from its inverse."],
             panel=lambda ax: sq.schematics.text_panel(ax, [r"$E_C=\dfrac{e^2}{2C_\Sigma}$"]), tools=["em"]),
        dict(title="Hamiltonian", lines=["Write every term and keep", "three levels per mode."], panel=hamiltonian,
             tools=["pen"]),
        dict(title="Readout", lines=[r"Size $\kappa$ near $2|\chi|$ and", "check the Purcell limit."], panel=readout,
             tools=["code", "vna"]),
        dict(title="Loss budget", lines=["Add surface losses and", "Purcell decay in series."], panel=losses,
             tools=["em", "stats"]),
        dict(title="Fabricate", lines=["Write the mask; probe the", "junctions at room temperature."],
             panel=spread, tools=["probe"]),
        dict(title="Validate", lines=["Compare prediction and", r"measurement; refit $E_J$."], panel=validate,
             tools=["fridge", "adc"]),
    ]
    side = [dict(after=2, title="Optional: tunable qubit", lines=["Replace the junction by a SQUID", "and budget flux noise."]),
            dict(after=3, title="Optional: package", lines=["Simulate the enclosure; keep", "its modes above the band."])]
    return sq.schematics.recipe_grid(None, steps, ncol=4, side=side)["fig"]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sq.demo_main(build, __file__)

"""A generic validation guide in two columns: the numbered steps run down each column with a mini-plot beside the text and the tools as labelled chips, and two optional steps sit in dashed side boxes joined to their step."""
import numpy as np

import scqfig as sq

TITLE = "Step guide"
FAMILY = "Schematics"


def calibrate(ax):
    lj = np.linspace(6, 16, 100)
    f = lambda L: 5.0 * np.sqrt(10 / L)
    ax.axvspan(9.2, 10.8, color=sq.theme().light, lw=0)
    ax.plot(lj, f(lj), **sq.model_kw())
    ax.plot(10, f(10), **sq.sim_kw(ms=3.5))
    ax.set(xlim=(6, 16), xticks=[8, 12, 16], yticks=[4, 6], xlabel=r"$L_J$ (nH)")


def strip(ax, spread, labels):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    for i, s in enumerate(spread):
        ax.plot(i + rng.uniform(-0.18, 0.18, 9), 1 + rng.normal(0, s, 9), **sq.data_kw(ms=2.5))
    ax.axhline(1, **sq.ref_kw())
    ax.set(xlim=(-0.5, len(spread) - 0.5), xticks=range(len(spread)), xticklabels=labels, ylim=(0.8, 1.2),
           yticks=[0.9, 1.1])
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=0)


def lifetimes(ax):
    t = sq.theme()
    pred, meas = [40, 25, 60], [18, 15, 22]
    for i, (p, m) in enumerate(zip(pred, meas)):
        ax.plot([i, i], [m, p], color=t.reference, lw=0.8)
        ax.plot(i, p, **sq.sim_kw(ms=3.2))
        ax.plot(i, m, **sq.data_kw(ms=3.2))
    ax.set(yscale="log", ylim=(8, 100), xlim=(-0.6, 2.6), xticks=[], ylabel=r"$T_1$ ($\mu$s)")
    ax.minorticks_off()


def misses(ax):
    t = sq.theme()
    ax.bar(range(3), [1.5, 12, 80], 0.55, color=t.light, ec=t.ink, lw=0.5, log=True)
    ax.set(ylim=(0.5, 300), xticks=range(3), xticklabels=["$f$", "$g$", "$T_1$"], ylabel="miss (%)")
    ax.minorticks_off()


def drift(ax):
    d = np.linspace(-5, 5, 50)
    ax.axvspan(-2, 2, color=sq.theme().tint, lw=0)
    ax.plot(d, -25 * d, **sq.model_kw())
    ax.set(xlim=(-5, 5), xticks=[-4, 0, 4], yticks=[-100, 100], xlabel=r"$\delta L_J$ (%)")


def build():
    steps = [
        dict(title="Calibrate the junction", lines=[r"Fit $L_J$ to the measured $f_{01}$", "and keep both values."],
             panel=calibrate, tools=["probe station", "VNA"]),
        dict(title="Compare frequencies", lines=["Qubit and resonator should", "agree within a few per cent."],
             panel=lambda ax: strip(ax, [0.02, 0.01], ["qubit", "res."]), tools=["spectroscopy"]),
        dict(title="Test the couplings", lines=["Fit $g$ from the avoided", r"crossing, not from $\chi$."],
             panel=lambda ax: strip(ax, [0.06], ["$g$"]), tools=["flux sweep", "EM solver"]),
        dict(title="Test the lifetimes", lines=["Set $T_1$ against a dielectric", "plus Purcell budget."],
             panel=lifetimes, tools=["$T_1$ decay"]),
        dict(title="Rank the misses", lines=["Order the quantities by", "how far the model missed."],
             panel=misses, tools=["statistics"]),
        dict(title="Report", lines=["State every convention and", "the inputs you assumed."], panel=None,
             tools=["paper draft"]),
    ]
    side = [dict(after=1, at="left", title="Optional: ageing", lines=["Junctions drift after", "fabrication."],
                 panel=drift, tools=["re-probe"]),
            dict(after=3, at="left", title="Optional: hybrid solve", lines=["Resolve the edge fields", "for surface losses."])]
    res = sq.schematics.recipe_grid(None, steps, ncol=2, order="column", plot="right", box=(2.55, 1.36),
                                    gap=(0.22, 0.3), side=side, side_width=1.32)
    return res["fig"]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sq.demo_main(build, __file__)

FQ, ALPHA, FR, G = 5.200, -0.210, 7.100, 0.090    # GHz


def build():
    t = sq.theme()
    q = t.qubits[0]
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(sq.WIDTHS["page"], 3.9))

              color=q, brace="transmon: junction and shunt capacitor"),
         "$+$",
         dict(text=rf"${FR:.3f}\,a^\dagger a$", kind="inductive", color="bus", brace="readout resonator")],
        ["$+$",
         dict(text=rf"${G:.3f}\,(a^\dagger b+a\,b^\dagger)$", kind="coupling",

                                   (r"assumed: $T_1$, $T_2^*$, readout fidelity", "reference")],

"""Xmon cell drawn to scale: a claw couples the quarter-wave resonator, a mask-level SQUID bridges the bottom gap, and two circular magnifiers show the claw and the SQUID, still to scale (designed geometry)."""
import scqfig as sq
from scqfig.schematics import chip, symbols

TITLE = "Mask cell with magnifiers"
FAMILY = "Schematics"

ARM, WIDTH, GAP = 170.0, 24.0, 24.0               # Xmon arm (tip from centre), arm width, gap, in um
W_RES, G_RES = 12.0, 8.0                          # resonator and claw CPW
V_FEED = 736.0                                    # feedline centre
WINDOW = (-420.0, -300.0, 840.0, 1120.0)          # u0, v0, w, h of the drawn part of the chip


def cell(ax):
    """The whole cell in chip units; the magnifiers call it again and show part of it enlarged."""
    u0, v0, w, h = WINDOW
    chip.substrate(ax, w, h, u0=u0, v0=v0)
    chip.ground_plane(ax, w, h, margin=0.0, u0=u0, v0=v0)
    q = chip.xmon(ax, 0.0, 0.0, arm=ARM, width=WIDTH, gap=GAP, squid=False)
    c = chip.claw(ax, *q["top"], arm=WIDTH, clearance=20.0, depth=80.0, w=W_RES, gap=G_RES)
    chip.meander_resonator(ax, 0.0, V_FEED - 36.0, c["attach"][1], couple=300.0, width=240.0, turns=4,
                           w=W_RES, gap=G_RES, side=1)
    chip.cpw(ax, [(u0, V_FEED), (u0 + w, V_FEED)], w=W_RES, gap=G_RES)
    s = chip.squid_detail(ax, 0.0, -ARM - GAP / 2, span=GAP, loop=(16.0, 8.0), lead=1.5, jj=0.5)
    return c, s


def build():
    t = sq.theme()
    fig, ax = sq.figure("column", aspect=0.93)
    symbols.blank(ax)
    c, s = cell(ax)
    claw_at = (c["tip"][0], (c["left"][1] + c["attach"][1]) / 2)
    # each magnifier redraws the cell; its scale bar sits above the disc, magnified by the same factor
    for at, r_at, centre, r, bar, name in ((claw_at, 80.0, (700.0, 470.0), 200.0, 20.0, "claw"),
                                           (s["center"], 22.0, (700.0, -60.0), 170.0, 5.0, "SQUID")):
        z = chip.zoom_circle(ax, at, r_at, centre, r, lambda ax, zoom: cell(ax), label=name)
        L = bar * z["scale"]
        chip.scale_bar(ax, centre[0] - L / 2, centre[1] + r + 30.0, L, label=f"{bar:g} µm")
    chip.scale_bar(ax, -400.0, -350.0, 200.0, below=True)
    kw = dict(fontsize=t.size - 1, zorder=9)
    ax.text(-ARM - 20.0, 40.0, "Xmon", ha="right", va="bottom", color=t.qubits[0], **kw)
    ax.text(-400.0, V_FEED + 26.0, "feedline", ha="left", va="bottom", color=t.chip["feedline"], **kw)
    ax.text(150.0, 420.0, r"$\lambda/4$", ha="left", va="center", color=t.chip["resonator"], **kw)
    ax.set_xlim(-430.0, 910.0)
    ax.set_ylim(-420.0, 830.0)
    return fig

    sq.demo_main(build, __file__)

"""Resonator-free bowtie sensor: (a) the two wedge islands to scale beside a feedline, with a charge line below and a schematic magnifier on the junction; (b) its circuit, with the gate set by a dc source through C_g (designed geometry)."""
from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle

import scqfig as sq
from scqfig.schematics import chip, symbols

TITLE = "Bowtie sensor"
FAMILY = "Schematics"

FIN, OPENING, SEP, POCKET = 110.0, 157.5, 12.0, 40.0     # fin radius, opening angle (deg), island gap, pocket, um
FEED_SEP = 60.0                                          # fin tip to feedline edge


def junction_inset(ax, zoom):
    """Inside the magnifier, in disc units: two electrode fingers overlapping at a small junction."""
    t = sq.theme()
    (cx, cy), r = zoom.center, zoom.r
    w = 0.22 * r
    for sgn in (1, -1):
        y0 = cy + sgn * 0.14 * r
        ax.add_patch(Rectangle((cx - w / 2, min(y0, y0 + sgn * r)), w, r, fc=t.qubits[1], ec="none"))
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((cx - 0.04 * r, cy - 0.16 * r), 0.08 * r, 0.32 * r, fc=t.qubits[1], ec="none"))
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((cx - 0.08 * r, cy - 0.08 * r), 0.16 * r, 0.16 * r, fc=t.chip["junction"], ec="none"))


def plan(ax):
    t = sq.theme()
    symbols.blank(ax)
    u0, v0, w, h = -300.0, -470.0, 600.0, 760.0
    chip.substrate(ax, w, h, u0=u0, v0=v0)
    chip.ground_plane(ax, w, h, margin=0.0, u0=u0, v0=v0)
    b = chip.bowtie(ax, 0.0, 0.0, fin=FIN, opening=OPENING, sep=SEP, gap=POCKET, angle=90.0, color=t.qubits[1])
    wf, gf = 16.0, 10.0
    vf = b["right"][1] + FEED_SEP + wf / 2                 # the fins point along v at angle = 90
    chip.cpw(ax, [(u0, vf), (u0 + w, vf)], w=wf, gap=gf)
    chip.drive_line(ax, [(0.0, v0), (0.0, b["left"][1] - 210.0)], w=10.0, gap=6.0)
    z = chip.zoom_circle(ax, b["junction"], 22.0, (470.0, -190.0), 130.0, junction_inset, magnify=False,
                         label="junction")
    chip.scale_bar(ax, 180.0, -440.0, 100.0)
    kw = dict(fontsize=t.size - 1, zorder=9)
    ax.text(u0 + 10.0, vf + 22.0, "feedline", ha="left", va="bottom", color=t.chip["feedline"], **kw)
    ax.text(14.0, v0 + 60.0, "charge line", ha="left", va="center", color=t.chip["drive"], **kw)
    # anchors rotate with the bowtie: at angle = 90 its local top is the left side of the pocket
    ax.text(b["pocket_top"][0] - 8.0, -60.0, "island", ha="right", va="center", color=t.qubits[1], **kw)
    ax.set_xlim(u0 - 10.0, 610.0)
    ax.set_ylim(v0 - 10.0, v0 + h + 10.0)
    return z


def circuit(ax):
    t = sq.theme()
    symbols.blank(ax)
    q, bus, gate = t.qubits[1], t.chip["feedline"], t.chip["drive"]
    fs = t.size - 0.5
    yt, yn, x1, x2, xg = 3.0, 1.7, 1.1, 2.7, 3.55
    symbols.wire(ax, [0.2, 3.9], [yt, yt], color=bus, lw=1.4)
    ax.text(0.2, yt + 0.12, "feedline", ha="left", va="bottom", fontsize=fs, color=bus)
    with symbols.tiles():
        for x, name in ((x1, r"$C_{c1}$"), (x2, r"$C_{c2}$")):
            symbols.wire(ax, [x, x], [yt, yn], color=q)
            symbols.capacitor_v(ax, x, 2.35, gap=0.1, w=0.3, color=q, tile_kind="coupling")
            ax.text(x - 0.25, 2.35, name, ha="right", va="center", fontsize=fs, color=q)
        symbols.wire(ax, [x1, x2], [yn, yn], color=q)
        symbols.junction(ax, (x1 + x2) / 2, yn, s=0.09)
        xm = (x1 + x2) / 2
        symbols.wire(ax, [x1, x1, xm - 0.05], [yn, yn - 0.6, yn - 0.6], color=q)
        symbols.wire(ax, [xm + 0.05, x2, x2], [yn - 0.6, yn - 0.6, yn], color=q)
        symbols.capacitor_h(ax, xm, yn - 0.6, gap=0.1, h=0.28, color=q)
        symbols.wire(ax, [x2, xg], [yn, yn], color=q)
        symbols.wire(ax, [xg, xg], [yn, 0.62], color=gate)
        symbols.capacitor_v(ax, xg, 1.2, gap=0.1, w=0.28, color=gate, tile_kind="coupling")
    ax.text(xm, yn + 0.16, r"$E_J$", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=fs, color=q)
    ax.text(xm, yn - 0.82, r"$C_\Sigma$", ha="center", va="top", fontsize=fs, color=q)
    ax.text(xg + 0.24, 1.2, r"$C_g$", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=fs, color=gate)
    symbols.dc_source(ax, xg, 0.45, r=0.17, color=gate)
    ax.text(xg + 0.26, 0.45, r"$V_g$", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=fs, color=gate)
    symbols.wire(ax, [xg, xg], [0.28, 0.12], color=gate)
    symbols.ground(ax, xg, 0.12, color=gate)
    ax.set_xlim(0.0, 4.3)
    ax.set_ylim(-0.1, 3.5)


def build():
    fig, (axa, axb) = sq.figure("page", aspect=0.5, ncols=2, width_ratios=[1.2, 1.0])
    plan(axa)
    circuit(axb)
    sq.panel(axa, "a")
    sq.panel(axb, "b")
    return fig


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sq.demo_main(build, __file__)

"""(a) Coupling graphs of five chip topologies: two qubits without a coupler, a chain, a star, a shared bus and a 2 x 3 lattice. (b) The four-qubit chain's sensing circuit, each wire in its qubit's colour: GHZ encoding, a shaded exposure window where a field acts on every wire at once, decoding and readout."""
import scqfig as sq
from scqfig.schematics import QCircuit, chip, symbols

TITLE = "Topologies and a coloured circuit"
FAMILY = "Schematics"

GRAPHS = [  # name, positions, couplings, keyword options
    ("pair", [(-1.0, 0.0), (1.0, 0.0)], [], dict(dashed=[(0, 1)])),
    ("chain", [(-2.1, 0.0), (-0.7, 0.0), (0.7, 0.0), (2.1, 0.0)], [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3)], {}),
    ("star", [(0.0, 0.0), (-1.2, 0.9), (1.2, 0.9), (-1.2, -0.9), (1.2, -0.9)], [(0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 3), (0, 4)], {}),
    ("bus", [(-1.2, 0.9), (1.2, 0.9), (-1.2, -0.9), (1.2, -0.9)], [], dict(hub=(0.0, 0.0))),
    ("lattice", [(-1.4, 0.8), (0.0, 0.8), (1.4, 0.8), (-1.4, -0.8), (0.0, -0.8), (1.4, -0.8)],
     [(0, 1), (1, 2), (3, 4), (4, 5), (0, 3), (1, 4), (2, 5)], {}),
]


def protocol(colors):
    c = QCircuit(4, labels=[r"$|0\rangle$"] * 4, wire_colors=colors)
    c.gate("H", 0)
    for k in range(3):
        c.cnot(k, k + 1)
    c.gate("H", [0, 1, 2, 3])
    c.gate(r"$U_\mathrm{DM}$", [0, 1, 2, 3], kind="plain", fill=sq.theme().wash)
    c.gate("H", [0, 1, 2, 3])
    for k in (2, 1, 0):
        c.cnot(k, k + 1)
    c.gate("H", 0)
    c.measure([0, 1, 2, 3])
    c.window(5, label=r"exposure $t_\mathrm{exp}$")
    return c


def build():
    t = sq.theme()
    colors = list(t.qubits[:4])
    c = protocol(colors)
    cw, ch = c.figsize(scale=0.33)
    fig, (axa, axb) = sq.figure("page", height=ch + 1.25, nrows=2, height_ratios=[1.0, ch / 1.05])
    symbols.blank(axa)
    for k, (name, pos, edges, opts) in enumerate(GRAPHS):
        x0 = 6.0 * k
        P = [(x0 + x, y) for x, y in pos]
        if "hub" in opts:
            opts = dict(opts, hub=(x0 + opts["hub"][0], opts["hub"][1]))
        chip.coupling_graph(axa, P, edges, r=0.3, colors=colors if name == "chain" else None, **opts)
        axa.text(x0, -1.65, name, ha="center", va="top", fontsize=t.size - 0.5, color=t.ink)
    axa.set_xlim(-3.0, 27.0)
    axa.set_ylim(-2.3, 1.4)
    c.draw(axb)
    sq.panel(axa, "a")
    sq.panel(axb, "b")
    return fig


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sq.demo_main(build, __file__)

examples.code:
"""Logarithmic sensitivities of a transmon's frequency, anharmonicity, coupling and dispersive shift to four design parameters (computed), and surface participation of two designs with the change printed over each pair (synthetic numbers)."""
import numpy as np

import scqfig as sq
from scqfig import physics as ph

TITLE = "Grouped bars"
FAMILY = "Comparison"

NOMINAL = {"C": 90.0, "LJ": 12.0, "Cg": 5.0, "fr": 7.2}       # fF, nH, fF, GHz


def outputs(C, LJ, Cg, fr):
    """f01, alpha, g and chi (GHz) of a transmon read out by a resonator at fr."""
    EJ, EC = 163.47 / LJ, 19.37 / C
    f01, alpha = np.sqrt(8 * EJ * EC) - EC, -EC
    n0 = NOMINAL
    EJ0, EC0 = 163.47 / n0["LJ"], 19.37 / n0["C"]
    g = 0.1 * (Cg / n0["Cg"]) * (n0["C"] / C) * ((EJ / EC) / (EJ0 / EC0)) ** 0.25 * np.sqrt(fr / n0["fr"])
    return f01, alpha, g, ph.dispersive_shift(f01, fr, g, alpha)


def build():
    sens = {}
    for p, label in (("C", r"$C_\Sigma$"), ("LJ", r"$L_J$"), ("Cg", r"$C_g$"), ("fr", r"$f_r$")):
        up, dn = dict(NOMINAL), dict(NOMINAL)
        up[p] *= 1.01
        dn[p] /= 1.01
        sens[label] = (np.log(np.abs(outputs(**up))) - np.log(np.abs(outputs(**dn)))) / (2 * np.log(1.01))
    fig, (a, b) = sq.figure("page", aspect=0.32, ncols=2, gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.3, 1]})
    sq.plots.grouped_bars(a, [r"$f_{01}$", r"$\alpha$", r"$g$", r"$\chi$"], sens)
    a.set_ylabel(r"$\partial\ln X/\partial\ln p$")
    regions = ["metal-air", "metal-substrate", "substrate-air"]
    sq.plots.grouped_bars(b, regions, {"design A": [2.1e-6, 3.2e-5, 4.0e-4], "design B": [9.5e-6, 1.1e-4, 4.4e-4]},
                          log=True, ratios=True, legend="upper left")
    b.set_ylabel(r"surface participation $p_i$")
    return fig

    sq.demo_main(build, __file__)

why.text: Each group restyles them by hand, and the restyling rarely survives the next paper.

scqfig draws each of them in a consistent house style, at print size, from data you pass in.
Levels, wavefunctions, chevrons, Wigner functions and response curves come from solvers in
`scqfig.physics`, not from sketches.

install.code:
git clone https://github.com/BoltzmannEntropy/scqfig.git && cd scqfig
pip install -e .            # from a checkout
pip install -e ".[test]"    # with pytest

install.text: scqfig is not on PyPI yet, so install it from a checkout of this repository.

It needs Python 3.9, numpy 1.22, scipy 1.8 and matplotlib 3.6, or any later version of each. LaTeX
is optional; you need it for the gallery PDF and for `usetex=True`.

quickstart.code:
import numpy as np
import scqfig as sq

sq.use("folio")                                   # or "field"
t = np.linspace(0, 240, 41)
p = 0.93 * np.exp(-t / 48) + 0.03 + np.random.default_rng(0).normal(0, 0.01, t.size)

fig, ax = sq.figure("column", aspect=0.62)        # 3.4 in wide: drop in at \columnwidth
fit = sq.plots.t1_decay(ax, t, p)                 # draws data, fit and "T1 = 47.3 ± 0.6 µs"
sq.save(fig, "figures/t1")                        # figures/t1.pdf and figures/t1.png
print(fit["T"], fit.errors["T"])

Every plot function draws on an Axes you pass in and returns what you need next: the fit, the mesh
and colour bar, or the artists. Panels compose freely:
